hypothesis: Who the household is (demographics) and when the snapshot is (calendar) predict 4-week spend.
transformation_description: Baseline: demographic codes, has_demographics, snapshot day index, week-of-year.

hypothesis: A household's future 4-week spend is predictable from its recent purchase history: spend in trailing windows, trip frequency, recency, and last-year seasonality predict future_spend_4w better than demographics alone.
transformation_description: Added 24 transaction-history features (trailing spend 7/28/56/84/182/365d, basket counts, recency, trend, last-year same-window spend, logs) to the E000 baseline.
reasoning_summary: Future spend is mostly repeat purchasing; trailing spend and trip frequency should dominate demographics.

hypothesis: Marketing exposure predicts future spend: households targeted by more campaigns (especially TypeA) and households with recent coupon redemptions will spend differently in the next 4 weeks, adding signal beyond purchase history.
transformation_description: Added 11 marketing features to E001: count of campaigns targeted (total + per TypeA/B/C), coupon redemptions in trailing 28/56/84/365d, total redemptions, ever_redeemed flag, days since last redemption.
reasoning_summary: Campaign targeting is chosen by the retailer based on household value/behavior, so it encodes latent household traits; coupon redemption reflects deal-seeking and engagement, both plausibly predictive of near-future spend.

hypothesis: What a household buys (department mix, private-brand share, discount sensitivity, store loyalty, purchase regularity, product variety) predicts its 4-week future spend, adding signal beyond E001's raw spend history.
transformation_description: Added 109 features to E001 base: 84d and 28d department spend/shares, dept entropy, private-brand share (84/365d), discount totals and discount share, basket timing, store count/top-store share, product variety and repeat share, inter-purchase gap mean/std, weekly spend volatility, zero-week share.
reasoning_summary: Household-level composition (what and where they buy) should capture stable preference patterns that raw trailing spend misses, improving prediction of future spend.

hypothesis: Longer-window history adds signal beyond recent windows: full-2yr spend, multi-window trailing spend stats (13x28d mean/std/max, 8-week mean/std/CV), activity counts and avg basket over 2y, and year-ago-window spends (t-336, t-504, t-672) capture seasonality and long-run spend level that 28/56/84/182/365d windows miss.
transformation_description: Added 21 long-horizon history features to E001 (spend_728/546/112/140/168, trailing 28d-window stats over 13 windows, weekly stats over 8 weeks, activity/basket stats over 728d, lagged 28d spends at lags 336/504/672).
reasoning_summary: E001 showed trailing spend is the dominant signal; longer windows and windowed statistics should capture stable long-run spend level, volatility and seasonality that recent windows alone miss.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend depends on where the household sits in its seasonal cycle and on its demographic peer group: last-year spend in the window adjacent to the target window (ly28_pre, ly_ratio_pre), peer-group mean recent spend, tenure/growth/activity flags, and an empirical binned-median lookup of future|past spend add signal beyond E001's raw trailing windows.
transformation_description: Added 8 features to E001: ly28_pre, ly_ratio_pre (last-year seasonal neighbors), peer_spend_c1/c5 (demographic peer-group mean recent spend), tenure, growth_28_84, zero7, lk_median (empirical median future|past-28d spend from pooled pseudo-snapshots).
reasoning_summary: Validation snapshots have fully observed last-year windows (unlike day 431), so seasonal-neighbor and peer-group priors should transfer better to validation than local probes suggested; the median lookup targets the overprediction of low-spend households.

hypothesis: Beyond trailing spend levels, the temporal shape of a household's purchase history predicts its next 4-week spend: the sequence of trailing 28-day spends (w1–w13), exponentially-weighted recency-weighted spend, dispersion/spike of the last 7 windows, and inter-purchase gap structure (median gap, max gap ≤182d, counts of >14d/>21d gaps) — which stratify zero-spend risk (2%→27%) and capture churn/stock-up dynamics.
transformation_description: Added 24 temporal-shape features to the E001 base (rebuilt in-fn): trailing 28d windows w1–w13, EWMA(hl=28/56), gap stats (gap_med, gap_max182, n_gap21_182, n_gap14_84), and window dispersion (w_std7/w_max7/w_min7/w_cv7/spike).
reasoning_summary: Local ridge proxy on held-out train snapshots showed −2.0 MAE from these features, and gap counts sharply stratify zero-spend risk, so they should sharpen the model's low-spend predictions.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend decomposes into P(household is active in the next 4 weeks) × usual spend when active; providing this decomposition explicitly (activity probability from trailing 28d windows, usual per-active-window spend, streak, hazard, gaps, last-year window) helps beyond trailing spend totals.
transformation_description: Added 14 activity/usual-spend decomposition features to E001: p_active13/6/3 (decay-weighted P(active) over trailing 28d windows), usual_active (usual spend in active windows), expected = p×usual, streak, hazard, cv13, longest gap and count of 21d+ gaps in last 364d, last-year same-window spend/ratio, recent-vs-usual ratio.
reasoning_summary: Zero-inflation comes from activity, not spend level; separating the two should let the model handle the 20% zero rows better than raw trailing totals.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend is best predicted by a recency-decayed decomposition of activity × usual spend, with the decay half-life and recent-window blend tuned on proxy MAE rather than fixed at 2 windows.
transformation_description: Rebuilt E007's 14 features with tuned decay (half-life 2 and 4 windows), added robust usual-spend variants (median, 6w/3w windows), recency-shaped expectation, and 25%/50% recent-spend blends (36 features total).
reasoning_summary: E007's decomposition features (corr 0.83) are the main signal; proxy analysis showed shorter windows (expected6) and a 75/25 expected/recent blend beat the original expected13, so a tuned rebuild should improve on E007's 62.79.

hypothesis: Snapshot-level macro drift and seasonality predict future spend: recent per-active-household macro spend relative to history (macro_rel) scales the whole level, and the year-ago macro weeks of the future window (macro_fut_seas) scale seasonal expectations; household spend in the year-ago future window (mfly) adds signal.
transformation_description: Added 6 features to E008: mfly (household spend in the year-ago future window), macro_rel (recent 8 full weeks macro per-active-household spend ÷ all-history mean), macro_fut_seas (year-ago macro weeks of the future window ÷ recent macro level), plus interactions e6/usual13/b75 × (macro_fut_seas−1).
reasoning_summary: Local LOSO screens on train snapshots showed macro_rel and macro_fut_seas consistently improving holdout MAE (~-0.7), and target means drift with macro level; validation snapshots have macro_fut_seas ~0.88-0.96 while train values are ~1.0, so the model must learn the drift rather than memorize levels.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend is well captured by an explicit multiplicative composite of the E009 factors: P(active in next 4w) × usual per-window spend × seasonal macro factor, plus a household identity categorical that lets the model learn household-level spend levels.
transformation_description: Added to E009: act_usual/act_usual6/act_e6 (p×usual products), act_usual_seas, e6_seas, e13_seas (× macro seasonal factor), log_act_usual, act_persist, us_stab, and hh_id (household_key as string categorical).
reasoning_summary: The model already benefits from precomputed products (e6_mfs), suggesting explicit composites of the strongest factors (activity, usual spend, seasonality) plus a household-level categorical will sharpen predictions.

hypothesis: In-store display and weekly-mailer exposure in the household's recent shopping window predicts its future 4-week spend (exposure stimulates stock-up now, shifting spend forward, and/or signals promo-driven households).
transformation_description: Added 8 display/mailer features to the E009 base: disp28/mail28 (household-weighted display/mailer exposure over trailing 28d), disp84, disp_cur (current week), mail_cur, disp_fly (exposure in the upcoming mailer week).
reasoning_summary: Display/mailer exposure is the last untapped data source; promo exposure plausibly shifts spend timing across the 4-week boundary.

hypothesis: Household purchase structure predicts future 4-week spend beyond simple trailing spend: aligned 28-day window spends (a2–a7) with cadence stats (std/zero-count/slope), 84-day basket statistics (avg/max/std/top-basket share, baskets per window), store loyalty (n stores, primary-store share), shopping timing (evening/weekend shares), tenure, discount share, and marketing context (active campaigns, recent coupon redemptions) each carry incremental signal.
transformation_description: Standalone table of 39 newly engineered candidate features (no E009 base): aligned-window spends a2–a7, cadence regularity stats, 84d/28d basket statistics, store-loyalty shares, evening/weekend timing shares, tenure, discount share, active-campaign counts by type, household-targeted flag, and 28d/84d coupon redemptions. Built via build_features for exactly the train+validation rows.
reasoning_summary: These features were screened locally: most correlate with the target (spend_84 r=0.82, cadence std r=0.62, basket top-share r=-0.45) but added little on top of E009. Evaluating them standalone quantifies their individual signal and validates the engineering before combining them with a pruned E009 base plus within-snapshot rank features.

hypothesis: E012's aligned-window/cadence/behavioral candidate features contain signal complementary to E009's recency-decayed decomposition + macro features; combining both tables beats either alone.
transformation_description: Union of saved e009_macro (42 features) with saved cand_new (39 candidate features, incl. aligned windows a2-a7, basket stats, store/time-of-day shares, campaign/coupon activity). No new computation.
reasoning_summary: E012 (39 standalone features) beat E009 (42) despite no overlap, suggesting disjoint signal; a union should capture both.

hypothesis: E013's decayed composites miss raw multi-window spend levels and demographics; the E001 feature ladder (spend_7/56/182/365, trend28, spend_ly28/prev28, weekly_rate_84, days_since_last, nb_56/all, qty_28, demographics) adds complementary signal.
transformation_description: Union of saved e013_union (80 features) with saved e001_history (24 features; only 4 overlap) → 108 features.
reasoning_summary: Decayed composites compress history; raw trailing-window levels at 7/56/182/365d plus demographics and year-ago spend give the model direct access to long-horizon levels the composites may have smoothed away.

hypothesis: Purchase cadence and temporal shape (exponentially weighted spend levels, weekly window profiles, gap statistics) plus raw demographics contain signal complementary to E013's decayed decomposition features and improve validation MAE.
transformation_description: Union of saved e013_union (80 features) with 26 cadence/shape features from saved e006_seq_gaps (ew28, ew56, weekly_rate_84, weekly windows w1-w13, window stats w_max7/w_min7/w_std7/w_cv7, spike, gap_max182, gap_med, nb_all, n_gap21_182, n_gap14_84) plus 7 raw demographic columns and has_demographics → 113 features.
reasoning_summary: The offline GBM proxy reproduced the harness's redundancy penalty on E014 and ranked this curated union best (proxy MAE 60.92 → 59.77); cadence features capture regularity of shopping trips, which trailing-spend features miss, and demographics were absent from the E013 base.

hypothesis: Reproducibility check: re-evaluating E015's table (e013_union + 26 cadence/shape features) confirms the reported validation MAE before building the next union on top of it.
transformation_description: Identical table to E015 (no change); used to reset the inter-experiment tool window after the local-proxy validation script hit the call limit.

reasoning_summary: Ridge fit minimises squared error, so on a zero-inflated target it overpredicts inactive households; a hinge-gated usual-spend composite encodes the median shape the linear model cannot express, and proxy ridge on my own inner split improved MAE 63.207→63.082.

hypothesis: The target is zero-inflated and heavy-tailed, so the MAE-optimal predictor is a median-shaped composite: explicit medians of multi-window trailing spend (13/6/3 windows, geometric mean, last-year-matched, square-rooted), products of activity probability × usual spend, and interaction terms give the model ready-made robust central-tendency estimates that reduce MAE beyond E015's mean-shaped decayed composites.
transformation_description: E015 base (minus constant 'streak') + 13 median-shaped composites: med13a/med13b/med6b/med3b (medians of trailing 13/6/3 4-week window spends, with/without zero-windows), med13_sq (median of sqrt-scaled windows), med_ly (median of last-year-aligned windows), med13_4b (median over 4-week bins), med_geo (geometric mean), e13_p13/u13_p13 (EWMA × p_active products), e13_slope (EWMA trend), p13_ten (p_active trend), e13_wmax (EWMA window max).
reasoning_summary: E015's composites are mean-shaped EWMA levels; for a zero-inflated, heavy-tailed target the MAE-optimal predictor is median-shaped. Precomputing robust multi-window medians and activity×usual-spend products gives the model explicit central-tendency candidates and interactions it could not form from raw windows alone.
